summary: range represents an integer arithmetic sequence without eagerly building a list.
documentation: range represents an integer arithmetic sequence without eagerly building a list. Its stop bound is excluded. Positive and negative steps work in opposite directions; zero step is invalid.
inputs: Integer start, exclusive stop and nonzero step.
returns: A range object representing the sequence.
caution: A range is not itself a JSON list. Materialize only reasonably bounded sequences before returning them.
scenarios: Generate numbered ticket slots for a small event.
Build row positions for a bounded table preview.
title: Generate a bounded sequence
problem: Input has integer start, stop and nonzero step. Return the values represented by range(start, stop, step) as a list. Inputs produce at most 100 items. The stop value is excluded.
goal: Use range() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Convert the range object to a list.
